problem.title: Exactly Three Spaces
problem.statement: Andrew wants to move exactly 3 spaces. Each move can advance him 1, 2, or 3 spaces. Two sequences are different if the move sizes occur in a different order. How many different sequences of moves can Andrew make?
hints: Try writing down sequences before deciding how to organize them.
How many moves could a valid sequence contain?

solutionSteps.title: Check every possible length
solutionSteps.body: Every move is positive, so a sequence totaling 3 has one, two, or three moves. Four moves would total at least 4. Each path has one length, so the total is 1 + 2 + 1 = 4.

notes: The move-count partition proves both exhaustiveness and non-overlap. There are no distractors because the response is open.

problem.title: Even-Sum Codes
problem.statement: A two-symbol code is formed using the digits 1, 2, 3, and 4. Repetition is allowed, and order matters. How many codes have an even digit sum?
hints: What parity combinations make an even sum?

solutionSteps.title: Find the two ways
solutionSteps.body: An even sum occurs when both digits are odd or both digits are even.

solutionSteps.title: Count odd-odd
solutionSteps.body: There are 2 choices for each position, giving 2 × 2 = 4 odd-odd codes.

solutionSteps.title: Combine
solutionSteps.body: Every code belongs to one of these two groups, never both, so the total is 4 + 4 = 8.

notes: The odd-odd and even-even cases are exhaustive and disjoint.

problem.title: Smaller Card on the Left
problem.statement: Two different cards are chosen from cards numbered 1 through 5 and placed in a left position and a right position. How many arrangements have the smaller number on the left?
hints: Split according to the card placed on the left.
If the left card is 3, how many right cards work?

solutionSteps.title: Case on the left card
solutionSteps.body: For left cards 1, 2, 3, 4, and 5, the number of larger choices on the right is respectively 4, 3, 2, 1, and 0.

solutionSteps.title: Combine the cases
solutionSteps.body: Each arrangement has exactly one left card, so the cases do not overlap. Their total is 4 + 3 + 2 + 1 + 0 = 10.

notes: The case totals 4, 3, 2, 1, and 0 independently sum to 10.

problem.title: Counters in Three Boxes
problem.statement: Five identical counters are placed into three labeled boxes A, B, and C, with at least one counter in each box. How many different distributions are possible?
hints: Split by how many counters are in Box A.
Once A is fixed, count the positive splits between B and C.

solutionSteps.title: A has one counter
solutionSteps.body: Then B and C receive 4 counters positively: (1, 3), (2, 2), or (3, 1), giving 3 distributions.

solutionSteps.title: A has two counters
solutionSteps.body: Then B and C receive 3 counters positively: (1, 2) or (2, 1), giving 2 distributions.

solutionSteps.title: A has three counters
solutionSteps.body: Then B and C must each receive 1 counter, giving 1 distribution.

solutionSteps.title: Combine
solutionSteps.body: A cannot contain more than 3 because B and C must remain nonempty. Every distribution appears in exactly one of these groups, so the total is 3 + 2 + 1 = 6.

validationMethods: exhaustive enumeration of positive integer triples

problem.title: A Six-Point Score
problem.statement: A game score of exactly 6 points is made using any number of 1-point, 2-point, and 5-point tokens. Only the number of each type matters. How many different token collections can make the score?
hints: How many 5-point tokens could the score contain?
After fixing the number of 5-point tokens, list the possible numbers of 2-point tokens.

solutionSteps.title: Use one 5-point token
solutionSteps.body: Then one 1-point token is forced, giving the collection 5 + 1.

solutionSteps.title: Use no 5-point tokens
solutionSteps.body: The number of 2-point tokens can be 0, 1, 2, or 3. The remaining points are filled by 1-point tokens, giving four collections.

solutionSteps.title: Combine the groups
solutionSteps.body: The groups contain 1 and 4 collections, so the total is 1 + 4 = 5.

notes: The number of 5-point tokens is either 0 or 1; the two groups list every collection exactly once.
